children: Inflation remains elevated, with the outlook continuing to be highly uncertain and risks tilted to the upside, according to Beth Hammack, CEO of the Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland.

Hammack gave opening remarks before the "Inflation: Drivers and Dynamics Conference 2026". The conference is hosted by the Center for Inflation Research at the Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland and the European Central Bank.

"The longer that high inflation persists, the more challenging and costly it can be to bring it back down," said the Federal Open Market Committee voting member. "Because monetary policy affects the economy with long and variable lags, we need a reliable way to separate temporary moves in inflation from changes that are more persistent."

According to Hammack, inflation expectations are central in models of inflation dynamics, and the monetary policy framework recognizes the importance of keeping those expectations well anchored at levels consistent with the 2% target.

title: Inflation risks are tilted to the upside, says Cleveland Fed's Hammack
